answer: A lantern test binds each agent identity to a costly, verifiable proof of work: before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it must complete a sequence of timed puzzles tied to a unique key, with its history publicly visible. Copying an identity is useless because the work cannot be duplicated for free, like a willow that bends but regrows only after real time passes. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents faces a thousand times the compute and delay, while a raven watching the ledger can spot the clones that never did the work. Cost scales with the attack, not with honest participation.
